Independent visitor's guide

# Visit Johannesburg: A Plain Guide to Joburg

Johannesburg is South Africa's biggest city and the place where much of its modern history was made. This guide shows you what to see, where to stay and eat, and how to get around safely.

[See things to do](https://example.com/things-to-do.html)[Getting around](https://example.com/getting-around.html)

## Johannesburg at a Glance

- **1,750 m**above sea level, so days are mild and nights can be cool
- **8**places to visit in this guide
- **6**neighbourhoods worth an afternoon
- **1886**the year gold was found on the Witwatersrand and the city began

## What to See When You Visit Johannesburg

Most visitors come for the history, stay for the food and music, and leave surprised by how green the city is. Here are three ways to spend your time.

### Learn the City's History

Start at the Apartheid Museum, then visit Constitution Hill, a former prison that now houses the Constitutional Court. In Soweto, walk down Vilakazi Street, where Nelson Mandela and Desmond Tutu both lived, and stop at the Hector Pieterson Memorial.

[See all things to do](https://example.com/things-to-do.html).

### Spend an Afternoon in a Neighbourhood

Joburg is a city of distinct areas, each with its own pace. Pick one or two and take your time.

- Braamfontein for its Saturday food market and rooftop bars
- Maboneng for street art, galleries and small shops
- Melville for cafés, bookshops and live music

[Compare the neighbourhoods](https://example.com/neighbourhoods.html).

### Get Outside

Johannesburg is often said to have one of the largest planted urban forests in the world. Walk in the Johannesburg Botanical Garden, picnic at Zoo Lake, or climb the Melville Koppies for a view over the northern suburbs. For a full day out, head to the Cradle of Humankind, a UNESCO World Heritage Site about an hour's drive away.

## Why Visit Johannesburg

Johannesburg is often a stop on the way to somewhere else. These are the reasons to give it a few days of its own.

### History You Can Stand In

- The places where South Africa's freedom struggle happened are open to visit, many with guides who lived through it.
### Food From Everywhere

- Try kota and shisa nyama in Soweto, Ethiopian coffee in the city centre and weekend markets across town.
### A Green City

- Millions of trees, parks and ridges. In spring, jacarandas turn whole streets purple.
### Easy to Reach

- O.R. Tambo is one of Africa's busiest airports, and the Gautrain links it to the city in about 15 minutes.
### Good Weather All Year

- Sunny winters and warm summers with short afternoon storms. Pack a jersey for the evenings.
### Music and Art

- Jazz, amapiano and theatre most nights, and galleries from the city centre to Rosebank.

## How to Plan Your Johannesburg Visit

1. Give the city two or three days. Add a day for the Cradle of Humankind or Pretoria.
2. Stay somewhere central to the Gautrain, such as Rosebank or Sandton, for an easy first trip.
3. Book a guided tour for Soweto and the city centre. Local guides know the stories and the streets.
4. Use ride-hailing apps at night, and keep your phone out of sight on the street.

Read the full [getting around guide](https://example.com/getting-around.html), or follow our [first-day plan](https://example.com/blog/first-day-in-johannesburg.html).

## Questions About Visiting Johannesburg

### When is the best time to visit Johannesburg?

Any time of year works. Summer (October to March) is warm, with short afternoon thunderstorms. Winter (June to August) is dry and sunny, with cold nights. In October and November, jacaranda trees turn many streets purple.

### Which airport serves Johannesburg?

O.R. Tambo International Airport (JNB), about 25 km east of the city centre. The Gautrain runs from the airport to Sandton, and from there to Rosebank and Park Station.

### What currency is used in Johannesburg?

The South African rand (ZAR). Cards are widely accepted. Carry a little cash for markets, tips and car guards.

### How many days do I need in Johannesburg?

Two or three days covers the main museums, Soweto and one or two neighbourhoods. Add a day for the Cradle of Humankind or Pretoria.

### Is Johannesburg safe for visitors?

Most visits pass without trouble if you take sensible care. Use ride-hailing or the Gautrain instead of walking at night, keep phones and bags out of sight, and go with a local guide in areas you do not know.

### Do I need a car in Johannesburg?

No. The Gautrain, ride-hailing apps and guided tours cover most of what visitors want to see. A car helps for day trips out of the city.

More answers on the [FAQ page](https://example.com/faq.html).

## Get the Joburg Weekend Email

One short email on a Thursday with markets, gigs and events for the weekend. No spam, and you can leave at any time.

Pick the places you want to see, check their hours, and plan your days around where you stay.

Things to do

# Things to Do in Johannesburg

These are the places we suggest for a first visit. Hours and prices change, so check each place's own website before you go.

## Museums, Landmarks and Day Trips

### Apartheid Museum

Ormonde

The story of apartheid and the struggle against it, told through film, photographs and personal accounts. Allow at least two to three hours.

- History
- Museum

[Open in Maps: Apartheid Museum](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2375,28.0103)

### Constitution Hill

Braamfontein

A former prison complex where Nelson Mandela and Mahatma Gandhi were held, now home to the Constitutional Court. Guided tours run through the day.

- History
- Architecture

[Open in Maps: Constitution Hill](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1889,28.0425)

### Vilakazi Street, Soweto

Orlando West, Soweto

The only street in the world where two Nobel Peace Prize winners lived: Nelson Mandela and Archbishop Desmond Tutu. Visit Mandela House and eat at one of the street's restaurants.

- History
- Food

[Open in Maps: Vilakazi Street, Soweto](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2385,27.9081)

### Hector Pieterson Memorial and Museum

Orlando West, Soweto

A memorial to the students killed in the Soweto uprising of 16 June 1976, a short walk from Vilakazi Street.

- History
- Museum

[Open in Maps: Hector Pieterson Memorial and Museum](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2381,27.9095)

### Cradle of Humankind

About 50 km northwest of the city

A UNESCO World Heritage Site with some of the world's richest fossil finds of early humans. Visit the Maropeng visitor centre and the Sterkfontein Caves. Plan a full day.

- Day trip
- Science
- Outdoors

[Open in Maps: Cradle of Humankind](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-25.9667,27.6622)

### Johannesburg Botanical Garden

Emmarentia

A large public garden with a rose garden, herb garden and walking paths beside Emmarentia Dam. Free to enter and good for a picnic.

- Outdoors
- Free

[Open in Maps: Johannesburg Botanical Garden](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1597,28.0028)

### Origins Centre

Braamfontein

A museum at Wits University about the origins of modern humans, with a large collection of southern African rock art.

- Science
- Museum

[Open in Maps: Origins Centre](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1925,28.03)

### Liliesleaf

Rivonia

The farm that served as a secret base for the liberation movement in the 1960s. The 1963 police raid here led to the Rivonia Trial.

- History
- Museum

[Open in Maps: Liliesleaf](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0442,28.0569)

## Tips for Your Visit

- Many museums close on Mondays. Check before you plan your week.
- The Apartheid Museum and Gold Reef City are next to each other, so you can visit both on one day.
- Soweto is best with a local guide. Walking and cycling tours start near Vilakazi Street.
- Leave a full day for the Cradle of Humankind. You need a car or a tour to get there.

Next: [choose a neighbourhood to explore](https://example.com/neighbourhoods.html).

---

Neighbourhoods

# Johannesburg Neighbourhoods to Explore

Joburg is spread out, so it helps to think of it as a set of smaller places. Pick one or two areas a day and travel between them by Gautrain or ride-hailing.

## Where to Go

### Braamfontein

A student district next to Wits University. Rooftop bars, galleries, coffee shops and a busy Saturday food market.

Good for: Food markets, nightlife, Constitution Hill

[Open in Maps: Braamfontein](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1929,28.0357)

### Maboneng

A small, walkable precinct on the east side of the city centre, known for street art, galleries, independent shops and restaurants.

Good for: Street art, galleries, weekend markets

[Open in Maps: Maboneng](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2044,28.0583)

### Soweto

South Africa's best-known township and the heart of much of the country's history. Go with a local guide to get the most from it.

Good for: History, Vilakazi Street, local food

[Open in Maps: Soweto](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2485,27.854)

### Melville

A relaxed suburb with a strip of cafés, bookshops and bars along 7th Street, close to the Melville Koppies nature reserve.

Good for: Cafés, live music, a walk on the koppies

[Open in Maps: Melville](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.175,28.008)

### Rosebank

A compact business and shopping district with its own Gautrain station, a weekend rooftop market and several galleries.

Good for: A first base, shopping, galleries

[Open in Maps: Rosebank](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.146,28.0436)

### Newtown

A cultural quarter in the west of the city centre, home to the Market Theatre and Mary Fitzgerald Square.

Good for: Theatre, music, history

[Open in Maps: Newtown](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.203,28.032)

## Where to Stay

For a first visit, stay in Rosebank or Sandton. Both have Gautrain stations, a good choice of hotels and restaurants within a short walk. Melville and Parkhurst have smaller guest houses with a quieter, local feel.

Next: [how to get around](https://example.com/getting-around.html).

Source: https://example.com/neighbourhoods.html


---

Transport and safety

# Getting Around Johannesburg

Johannesburg is large and spread out. Most visitors use the Gautrain for longer trips and ride-hailing apps for everything else.

## From the Airport

O.R. Tambo International Airport is about 25 km east of the city centre. The Gautrain airport line takes you to Sandton in about 15 minutes. Change at Sandton for Rosebank, Park Station and Pretoria. Ride-hailing cars and metered taxis wait outside the terminals.

## Gautrain

The Gautrain is a fast, clean rapid rail line that links the airport, Sandton, Rosebank, the city centre and Pretoria. Pay with a Gautrain card or a contactless bank card at the gates. Feeder buses run from most stations.

## Ride-Hailing and Taxis

Uber and Bolt both work well in Johannesburg and are the easiest way to travel door to door, especially at night. Check the number plate and the driver's name before you get in.

## Buses and Minibus Taxis

Rea Vaya is a bus rapid transit system with its own lanes, linking Soweto with the city centre. Minibus taxis carry most of the city's commuters. They are cheap but hard to use without local help, so ask a guide or your host first.

## Driving

South Africa drives on the left. A car is useful for day trips, such as the Cradle of Humankind. In the city, expect heavy traffic at rush hour and power cuts that can turn off traffic lights. Treat a dark traffic light as a four-way stop.

## Staying Safe

- Keep your phone, camera and bag out of sight on the street and in the car.
- Use ride-hailing instead of walking after dark, even for short trips.
- Go with a local guide in the city centre and in Soweto.
- Keep car doors locked and windows up at traffic lights.
- In an emergency, call 10111 for the police or 112 from a mobile phone.

Source: https://example.com/getting-around.html

About

# About Visit Joburg

Visit Joburg is an independent guide to Johannesburg for visitors. We want to help people see more of the city, with clear advice in plain words.

## What We Include

We list places we would send a friend to on their first visit. Nobody pays to be included. When we link to a business, it is because we think it is useful, and we do not earn a fee for it.

## Keeping It Accurate

Opening hours, prices and transport change often, so we do not list them. Each listing links to a map, and we ask you to check details with the place itself before you go. Each page shows the date we last reviewed it.

## Not an Official Body

Visit Joburg is not linked to the City of Johannesburg, the Gauteng Tourism Authority or South African Tourism.

## Suggest a Change

If something is wrong or missing, [tell us](https://example.com/contact.html). We read every message.

Last reviewed: 11 November 2026.

Source: https://example.com/about.html

Accessibility

# Accessibility Statement

We aim to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA on every page of this site.

## What We Do

- One main heading per page and headings in order.
- Landmarks for the header, navigation, main content and footer, and a skip link as the first thing in the tab order.
- Text contrast of at least 4.5 to 1 in both light and dark colour schemes.
- Visible focus on every link and control, and touch targets of at least 44 by 44 pixels.
- A text alternative for every image that carries meaning.
- Form fields with visible labels.
- No movement unless you ask for it, and support for reduced motion and forced colours.
- A menu that works with the keyboard. The Escape key closes it.

## How We Check

Every build runs automated checks on headings, images, links, forms and colour contrast. Before each release we also test with Lighthouse, axe and a screen reader.

## Tell Us About a Problem

Email hello@example.com. We reply within two working days.

Last reviewed: 11 November 2026.

Source: https://example.com/accessibility.html

Itinerary

# How to Spend Your First Day in Johannesburg

By the Visit Joburg team. Published 11 November 2026.

A first day in Johannesburg can feel like a lot. This plan keeps travel short, puts the history first and ends somewhere you can relax. It works best with a ride-hailing app or a booked driver.

## Morning: The Apartheid Museum

Arrive when the museum opens. The exhibits move from the start of apartheid to the first democratic election in 1994, and they take time to read and watch. Two to three hours is about right. Your entry ticket tells you which entrance to use, based on a racial category, so the visit starts with how apartheid divided people.

## Lunch: Vilakazi Street, Soweto

Take a short ride west to Soweto. Vilakazi Street has several restaurants serving South African food, from braaied meat to pap and chakalaka. After lunch, visit Mandela House, then walk to the Hector Pieterson Memorial. A local guide adds the stories you will not find on the signs.

## Afternoon: Constitution Hill

Head back towards the city centre for Constitution Hill. The old prison cells sit next to the Constitutional Court, which was built partly from the bricks of the demolished awaiting-trial block. Join a guided tour if you can.

## Evening: Braamfontein or Maboneng

Constitution Hill sits on the edge of Braamfontein, so you can end the day at a rooftop bar or a restaurant a few minutes away. If you prefer street art and small galleries, take a short ride to Maboneng instead. Either way, book your ride home rather than walking after dark.

## Before You Go

- Check opening days. Many museums close on Mondays.
- Carry a little cash for tips and small purchases in Soweto.
- Wear comfortable shoes and bring a jersey for the evening.

Want more ideas? See all [things to do in Johannesburg](https://example.com/things-to-do.html).

Source: https://example.com/blog/first-day-in-johannesburg.html
